gentle.title: Dim the lights half an hour before bed
gentle.detail: Soften the brightness around the house in the half hour before sleep. The body reads it as evening and slows down.

coach.title: Dim lights 30 min before bed
coach.detail: Drop overhead lighting thirty minutes before bedtime. Melatonin lifts cleanly when ambient light drops.

firm_direct.title: Lights low. 30 min before bed.
firm_direct.detail: Half hour before bed: kill overhead lights. Lamps only. Phone brightness down.

gentle.title: Half an hour of quiet before bed
gentle.detail: Soft music, a tidy of the kitchen, a cup of tea. A low-stimulation half hour before sleep.

coach.title: 30-minute quiet wind-down
coach.detail: Spend the last 30 minutes on low-stimulation activities — tea, light cleanup, soft music. Sleep onset eases.

firm_direct.title: Quiet 30 minutes. Pre-bed.
firm_direct.detail: Half hour before bed: no work, no doom-scroll, no high-stim TV. Tea. Tidy. Music low.

gentle.title: A small bedtime ritual tonight
gentle.detail: Three things you do every night, in the same order — wash up, dim the lights, climb in. Routines settle the body.

coach.title: Run your bedtime routine tonight
coach.detail: Same three steps, same order, every night. The sequence itself becomes a sleep cue.

firm_direct.title: Routine. Same order. Tonight.
firm_direct.detail: Wash up. Lights down. Bed. Same order, every night. Build the cue.

gentle.title: Bedtime within half an hour of usual
gentle.detail: Tonight, aim for your normal bedtime, give or take thirty minutes. Routine shows up in sleep quality.

coach.title: Bedtime within ±30 min of usual
coach.detail: Hit your normal bedtime within a half-hour window tonight. Circadian rhythm rewards consistency.

firm_direct.title: Bed. Usual time. ±30 min.
firm_direct.detail: Within thirty minutes of your normal bedtime. No drift. No 'just one more episode.'

gentle.title: Lights out at the same time tonight
gentle.detail: Whatever time you usually sleep — aim for the same tonight. The body settles into rhythm.

coach.title: Lights-out at your usual time
coach.detail: Match tonight's lights-out to your typical week. The rhythm is what carries the sleep, not just the duration.

firm_direct.title: Lights out. Usual hour.
firm_direct.detail: Same lights-out as a normal week night. Phone in dock. Eyes closed.

gentle.title: Wake up at the usual hour tomorrow
gentle.detail: Try not to sleep in much — even a small consistency helps the body line up its rhythm.

coach.title: Same wake time tomorrow
coach.detail: Set the alarm for your typical wake hour, even if it's the weekend. Wake-time consistency drives the next bedtime.

firm_direct.title: Wake. Usual hour. No drift.
firm_direct.detail: Alarm at your normal time. No snooze. Out of bed. Tomorrow's sleep starts here.

gentle.title: Make the bedroom a little cooler tonight
gentle.detail: Drop the thermostat a couple of degrees, or crack the window. Cool rooms sleep deeper.

coach.title: Cool the bedroom tonight
coach.detail: Set the bedroom around 65–68°F. Sleep architecture deepens; you spend more time in the restorative stages.

firm_direct.title: Bedroom. Cool tonight.
firm_direct.detail: Thermostat down a few degrees. Window cracked if needed. Cooler than the rest of the house.

gentle.title: A darker bedroom tonight
gentle.detail: Curtains pulled, a sleep mask if you have one, devices flipped face-down. Even small light leaks add up.

coach.title: Block more light tonight
coach.detail: Pull curtains tight, mask any device LEDs, sleep mask if needed. Darkness lifts melatonin further.

firm_direct.title: Room. Dark. Tonight.
firm_direct.detail: Curtains shut. LEDs covered. Sleep mask if you have one. No glow in the room.

gentle.title: A quieter bedroom tonight
gentle.detail: Earplugs, a fan, a white-noise track — whatever softens the sound layer. The body wakes less when it's quiet.

coach.title: Quiet the bedroom tonight
coach.detail: Add a sound buffer: earplugs, a fan, or white noise. Fewer micro-arousals, more continuous sleep.

firm_direct.title: Room. Quiet tonight.
firm_direct.detail: Earplugs. Fan. White noise app. Pick one. Use it tonight.

gentle.title: No caffeine after noon today
gentle.detail: Try moving the cutoff to noon. Tea after, water, decaf. Sleep tonight will feel different.

coach.title: Caffeine cutoff at noon
coach.detail: Last cup before noon. Caffeine's half-life is ~6 hours; the noon coffee still touches midnight sleep.

firm_direct.title: Caffeine off. Noon.
firm_direct.detail: Last cup before 12. After: water, herbal, decaf. Strict cutoff.

gentle.title: Make your last coffee a noon coffee
gentle.detail: If you'd usually have an afternoon cup, skip it today and see how sleep lands.

coach.title: Last coffee at noon today
coach.detail: Move the final coffee to lunchtime. Then water, tea, or decaf. Most people notice deeper sleep within nights.

firm_direct.title: Final coffee. Noon. Today.
firm_direct.detail: Last coffee at lunchtime. Afternoon: tea or water. No relapse cup at 3pm.

gentle.title: Switch to decaf in the afternoon
gentle.detail: Same warm-cup ritual, just decaffeinated. The flavor of the routine stays; the stimulant load drops.

coach.title: Decaf afternoon today
coach.detail: Keep the coffee ritual; swap to decaf in the afternoon. Same comfort, no carry-over to bedtime.

firm_direct.title: Afternoon. Decaf only.
firm_direct.detail: Cup at 3pm? Decaf. Cup at 5pm? Decaf. No regular after lunch.

gentle.title: Phone outside the bedroom tonight
gentle.detail: Charge it in the kitchen or hallway. The morning notifications can wait. Sleep gets deeper.

coach.title: Phone out of bedroom tonight
coach.detail: Charge the phone in another room. Removes the mid-night scroll temptation; reduces blue light at wake.

firm_direct.title: Phone. Other room. Tonight.
firm_direct.detail: Phone charges in the kitchen, hallway, anywhere not the bedroom. Alarm clock if needed. Done.

gentle.title: Screens off an hour before bed
gentle.detail: Phone, laptop, TV — off an hour before sleep. A book, a chat, a slow tea. The eyes thank you.

coach.title: Screens off 60 min before bed
coach.detail: All screens off an hour before bedtime. Blue light suppression flips back on; sleep onset shortens.

firm_direct.title: Screens off. 60 min before bed.
firm_direct.detail: Hour before bed: phone face-down, TV off, laptop closed. No exceptions tonight.

gentle.title: No screens once you're in bed
gentle.detail: If you read in bed, paper instead of screen. The bed stays a place for sleep, not for scrolling.

coach.title: Bed = no screens tonight
coach.detail: Once you're in bed, no phone, no tablet. Reading: paper-book or e-ink. Strengthens the bed-sleep association.

firm_direct.title: In bed. No screens.
firm_direct.detail: Pillow hits, screen down. Phone on dresser. Book if you read. Eyes closed otherwise.

gentle.title: Five gentle stretches before bed
gentle.detail: Forward fold, slow neck rolls, a quiet hip opener. Five minutes that softens the body before sleep.

coach.title: 5-min bedtime stretch
coach.detail: Five minutes of slow stretches before bed: forward fold, neck rolls, hip opener. Releases the day's tension.

firm_direct.title: Stretch. 5 min. Pre-bed.
firm_direct.detail: Forward fold. Neck rolls. One hip opener. Five minutes. Then bed.

gentle.title: A few minutes of slow breath before sleep
gentle.detail: In through the nose for four, out for six. Five minutes of slow breath as you settle in.

coach.title: 5-min slow breathing before bed
coach.detail: Four-in, six-out for five minutes. Activates the parasympathetic system; sleep onset eases.

firm_direct.title: Breathe slow. 5 min.
firm_direct.detail: In four. Out six. Five minutes. Lying down. Then sleep.

gentle.title: Three things from today, on paper
gentle.detail: Before lights out, write down three small things from today — anything good, anything noticed.

coach.title: Journal 3 things before bed
coach.detail: Three things from today, written quickly. Closes the mental open-loops that keep the brain busy at lights-out.

firm_direct.title: Three things. Paper. Pre-bed.
firm_direct.detail: Three lines about today. Pen, paper. Two minutes. Then sleep.

gentle.title: Skip a late-afternoon nap today
gentle.detail: If a tired wave hits after 4pm, a walk or a glass of water often does the job better than sleep.

coach.title: No naps after 4pm today
coach.detail: Late naps eat into nighttime sleep pressure. After 4pm: walk, water, light snack instead.

firm_direct.title: No naps. After 4pm.
firm_direct.detail: Tired at 4pm? Walk. Water. Snack. Don't lie down. Save it for bedtime.

gentle.title: Keep a nap to about twenty minutes
gentle.detail: If a nap lands today, set a small timer. Twenty minutes is the sweet spot — no grogginess after.

coach.title: Cap any nap at 20 minutes
coach.detail: Set a timer; twenty minutes max. Stops you from dropping into deep sleep, avoids the post-nap fog.

firm_direct.title: Nap. 20 min cap.
firm_direct.detail: Timer for twenty. No more. Get up when it rings. No second alarm.

gentle.title: If you nap, before 3pm
gentle.detail: Earlier naps don't compete with bedtime. Aim for before three if a rest is needed.

coach.title: Nap before 3pm only
coach.detail: Naps before mid-afternoon don't dent night sleep. Past 3pm: skip and ride it out.

firm_direct.title: Nap. Before 3pm. Or skip.
firm_direct.detail: If napping today: before 3pm. After that: skip. Walk it off.

gentle.title: Five minutes of morning daylight
gentle.detail: Step outside, or sit by a sunny window, in the first hour after waking. The day starts cleaner.

coach.title: 5-min morning sunlight
coach.detail: Five minutes of outdoor daylight in the first hour up. Anchors circadian rhythm; tonight's sleep gets the benefit.

firm_direct.title: Sun. 5 min. AM.
firm_direct.detail: First hour up: outside for five. No sunglasses, no hood. Light on the eyes.

gentle.title: Open the curtains right after waking
gentle.detail: First action after coffee, or before — let the daylight in. The body knows it's morning.

coach.title: Curtains open on rising
coach.detail: Open all curtains within minutes of getting up. Indoor light fast-tracks the wake-up signal.

firm_direct.title: Curtains. Open. AM.
firm_direct.detail: Out of bed, curtains open. Every window. Light in immediately.

gentle.title: A short outdoor walk in the morning
gentle.detail: Five minutes around the block before screens take over. The light counts; the movement counts more.

coach.title: 5-min outdoor walk after waking
coach.detail: Within an hour of waking, five minutes outdoors. Sunlight on the eyes plus light movement — circadian gold.

firm_direct.title: Walk. 5 min. Morning.
firm_direct.detail: First hour: shoes on, outside, walk five. No phone meeting on the way. Just light and feet.

gentle.title: No eating after nine tonight
gentle.detail: Last bite by nine. Tea or water after if hunger nudges. Sleep onset gets noticeably softer.

coach.title: No food after 9pm tonight
coach.detail: Stop eating by 9pm. Two-plus hours before bed lets digestion settle and sleep deepen.

firm_direct.title: No food. After 9pm.
firm_direct.detail: Kitchen closes at 9. Water and tea after. No sneaky snack.

gentle.title: Stop eating two hours before bed
gentle.detail: Whenever bedtime is, plan the last bite for two hours before. Digestion gets a head start; sleep gets deeper.

coach.title: Last bite 2 hours before bed
coach.detail: Set a personal kitchen-close two hours before bedtime. Reduces reflux risk; deepens sleep architecture.

firm_direct.title: Stop eating. 2 hours pre-bed.
firm_direct.detail: Whatever your bedtime: kitchen closes two hours before. Plan dinner accordingly.

gentle.title: A lighter dinner tonight
gentle.detail: If dinner runs late or sleep needs help, eat less than usual. The body falls asleep cleaner without a heavy load.

coach.title: Lighter dinner tonight
coach.detail: Eat smaller than usual at dinner. Big late meals sit on the chest at bedtime; smaller meals slip into sleep.

firm_direct.title: Dinner. Small tonight.
firm_direct.detail: Cut dinner portion. No heavy plate before bed. Save the big meal for lunch tomorrow.

gentle.title: Drink most of your water early today
gentle.detail: Front-load hydration before evening. Less water at night means fewer trips up at 3am.

coach.title: Front-load water before evening
coach.detail: Hit most of your water target by 6pm. Reduces overnight bathroom trips; sleep stays continuous.

firm_direct.title: Water. Front-loaded. Before 6pm.
firm_direct.detail: Hydrate hard before evening. After 6pm: small sips only. Fewer wake-ups tonight.

gentle.title: Less to drink in the last two hours
gentle.detail: Taper liquids in the two hours before bed. The body sleeps through better when the bladder is calm.

coach.title: Taper fluids 2 hours before bed
coach.detail: Cut down liquid intake in the last two hours. A few sips for thirst, but no full glasses. Continuous sleep follows.

firm_direct.title: Fluids. Taper. 2 hours pre-bed.
firm_direct.detail: Last two hours before bed: small sips only. No tea, no big water glass. Bladder settles.

gentle.title: Just small sips after seven tonight
gentle.detail: After 7pm, small sips when needed. Front-load the day's water; let the evening run light.

coach.title: Small sips only after 7pm
coach.detail: Past 7pm: small sips for thirst, no full glasses. Bladder calms; mid-night wake-ups drop.

firm_direct.title: After 7pm: sips only.
firm_direct.detail: Past seven: sips for thirst. No tea pot. No filling water bottles. Sleep through.
